And when this was confirmed,
he became angry with the Comitas and blinded his eyes.
Immediately Khosrow sent the Marzban Adramon,
and he plundered and took captive the region of Balash, Qinnasrin, and the territory of Antioch.
And because formerly, when the king of Persia came to Apamea,
the people had gone out to meet him,
and he entered and saw the bishop there,
and did not harm them;
for this reason, now also they went out to meet the Marzban wearing white garments.
And when he entered, he deceitfully plundered the city and burned it,
and persons, 292,
(292) [or] 92 thousand he sent to Persia.
At this time Khosrow chose two thousand virgins from the captives,
and adorned them and sent them to the Turks who were beyond Persia.
Now when they arrived within five stages of the Turks,
and encountered a large river,
they took counsel together to hasten to death,
so that they would not lose the faith that was in their souls and the purity of their bodies.
And having pledged their right hands to one another,
they asked the Persian guards to withdraw from them as if to bathe.
And they,
because they had been commanded to lead them gently so that their beauty would not be marred,
withdrew.
Then those modest maidens, having sealed their faces with the sign of the cross,
cried out in the name of Christ,
and cast themselves into that great river and drowned.
Now the guards, when they ran at the sound of their crying out
and saw them drowning,
struggled,
and were not able to rescue even one of them.
Now when the king of the Romans heard of these things that had happened,
he prepared to go down to the East;
and from the distress of his thoughts a demon came upon him.
And Zacharias was sent to Khosrow concerning peace,
and with him six hundred and fifty litras of gold,
for a peace of one year only.
And because at certain times his mind returned to him,
and he lamented over himself and wept bitterly,
the magnates advised him,
and he appointed a certain Greek secretary named Tiberius, a Thracian, as administrator of his kingdom,
and they proclaimed him Caesar.
At this time Khosrow was lifted up with pride,
and he came to Armenia,
and directed his course to Cappadocia to conquer Caesarea.
The Romans, however, overtook them at Mount Bagravand {OCR?}.
